title_content.content: Continuous Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Robot Navigation

Abstract—Autonomous navigation is one of the focuses in the field of mobile robot research. The traditional method usually consists of two parts: building the map of environment, localization of mobile robot and path planning. However, these traditional methods usually rely on high-precision sensor information. At the same time, mobile robots have no intelligent understanding of autonomous navigation. In this article, a deep reinforcement learning method, i.e. soft actor critic, is used to navigate in a mapless environment. It takes laser scanning data and information of the target as input, outputs linear velocity and angular velocity in continuous space. The simulation shows that this learning-based end-to-end autonomous navigation method can accomplish tasks as well as traditional methods.
Keywords—Mobile Robot, Deep Reinforcement Learning, Soft Actor Critic, Autonomous navigation

The use of mobile robots has been well popularized, such as delivery and rescue. Being able to navigate autonomously in a complex environment is a prerequisite for completing these tasks. In the traditional method, autonomous navigation can be divided into two parts. The first part is the localization and mapping of mobile robots. Mobile robots rely on various sensors to sense the external environment and their own postures. This process is called Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM) [1]. It uses the information of laser or camera sensor to build an obstacle map. The second part is path planning. The purpose of path planning is to plan a path from the starting point to the target point without collision. The main methods of path planning include heuristic search methods such as A-star algorithm [2], random sampling-based methods such as Rapidly-exploring Random Tree(RRT) [3] and the methods based control theory such as dynamic window approach [4]. Today, the traditional methods have matured. However, most of these methods are dependent on obstacle map, and the mobile robot does not have an intelligent understanding of the navigation problem. In addition, the traditional method is very dependent on high-precision sensors. Nowadays, there are already many indoor localization methods, such as UWB localization [5]. So the position of the mobile robot and the position of the target point can be got easily. In this case, it is important to propose a mapless navigation method.

Learning-based methods have been successfully applied to autonomous navigation. Imitate learning [6] and supervised learning [7] can get good results. This type of method works by training human-labeled data through deep neural networks.
Its drawback is obvious because it is limited by the amount of data.

Reinforcement learning is different from traditional supervised learning and unsupervised learning. It is a process in which an agent learns by interacting with the environment. It does not require human-labeled data. In 2011, Mohammad proposed using the Q-learning algorithm to solve the problem of robot navigation in an unknown environment [8]. However, limited to the size of the Q-learning state space, this method is not suitable for complex environments. In 2013, Mnih et al. proposed the basic method of deep reinforcement learning, Deep Q-Network (DQN) model [9]. Deep reinforcement learning deals with higher dimensional state spaces by introducing deep neural network to fitting value functions. Deep reinforcement learning is currently used in a variety of robot control applications. Tung-Cheng Wu et al. use depth images as input to complete the autonomous obstacle avoidance of drones [10]. Kendall et al. successfully applies deep reinforcement learning to autonomous driving, outputting continuous steering and speed commands [11]. Y. Zhu et al. proposed a target-driven deep reinforcement learning visual navigation method [12]. All of this work proves the effectiveness of deep reinforcement learning on robot autonomous navigation.

In recent years, lots of methods for deep reinforcement learning have been proposed. The DQN is a value-based method, so it can't satisfy the continuous action space. Lillicrap et al. combined the DQN method with the Actor-Critic policy gradient method and proposed the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), which extends it to the continuous action space[13]. Policy gradient based methods such as Trust region policy optimization (TRPO) [14] and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [15] can achieve better stability. Soft Actor Critic (SAC) [16] is an algorithm which optimizes a stochastic policy in an off-policy way, forming a bridge between stochastic policy optimization and DDPG-style approaches. It incorporates the clipped double-Q trick. And due to the inherent stochasticity of the policy in SAC, it also winds up benefiting from something like target policy smoothing. Therefore, SAC algorithm was chosen as the training algorithm in this paper. At the same time, the Robot Operating System (ROS) and Gazebo were used to simulate the virtual environment. Experiments show that the mobile robot can quickly learn the autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance policy.

item_content.content: - An continuous control method for autonomous navigation of mobile robots in mapless environment based on SAC algorithm is proposed.
- Inputs are low-dimensional laser scan data and target information. By this way, it can effectively reduce the resource required for calculation.
- In order to make full use of the previously observed states, actions and rewards, the LSTM [17] neural network is used to fit the value function and Q function.

title_content.content: C. State Space And Action Space

item_content.content: 1) State Space: In order to complete the task, the state space was defined as three parts. The first part is 10-dimensional laser scanning data with scanning angle 360 degrees. The second is the angle and distance between robot and target position. The third is the action selected at the last moment and the reward. The laser scanning data can help the robot learn to avoid obstacles, the information of the target point informs the goal of the robot navigation. The action and reward of the previous moment can more effectively make the robot learn the correctness of the current action.

2) Action Space: The action space consists of two dimensions, one for linear velocity and one for angular velocity. All of these velocity command is represented by a squashed Gaussian policy. A clip function is used to ensure the linear velocity is limited to

paragraph_content.content: In order to let the agent better understand the goal to learn, that is, to reach the target position as soon as possible without collision. The reward function of this paper is defined as follows: when the mobile robot collides, a negative reward of -100 is given. If the mobile robot reaches target position, a positive reward of +500 is provided.

When the mobile robot moves freely in the environment, the reward depends on the difference from the target position compared with last time step. For reaching the target as fast as possible, a reward of -3 is given for every time step.
Combined with the above four parts, the reward function is defined as:

paragraph_content.content: As shown in Fig. 2, the input of value network is a 15-dimensional vector that includes laser scanning data(10-dimensional), target position(2-dimensional, distance and angle), the action of last time step(2-dimensional) and reward(1-dimensional). In order to make the network have the memory of the previous observations and can learn the prediction of the motion, LSTM is chosen as the hidden layer with 512 nodes. After three hidden layers, the output is a state value function
, which is used to evaluate the quality of the state.

Q network is used to fit the Q value, which evaluate the quality of the action is taken in a certain state. The input consists of a state vector and an action vector, which we merge into a 17-dimensional vector. Similar to the value network, the final output is a one-dimensional Q value.

The policy network is used to generate a Gaussian distribution. After processing the input state vector through two fully connected layers, the mean and standard deviation are generated respectively. Then the action (2-dimensional velocity command) is generated according to the Gaussian distribution. The tanh activation function and clip operation are used to constrain the linear velocity in

The model was trained on a PC with Nvidia GeForce RTX 2070 GPU, 3.70 GHz eight core AMD Ryzen 7 2700X processor and 16 GB memory. The environment is speeded up 10 times to train. The training procedure took three hours.

The simulation results is shown in Fig. 4. It can be seen that the mobile robot always hits obstacles at the beginning and get a negative reward. With constant trial and error, the mobile robot learned the policy to complete the autonomous navigation task and approached convergence. For comparison, the LSTM layers in the value and Q network were replaced with fully-connected layer while other parameters remained unchanged. It can be seen that the mean reward of LSTM network has increased faster than fully-connected networks. The success rate is shown in Fig. 5. It can be seen that the success rate was increasing with the convergence of policy. Of course, as training time increases, the success rate will become higher and higher.

paragraph_content.content: 2) Evaluation: As shown in Fig. 7 and Fig. 8, seven targets were set for mobile robot. The robot's goal is to arrive these target points in turn. It is worth noting that for move_base, building a map is a prerequisite for path planning. But for reinforcement learning methods, maps are only used for visualization of paths. As shown in the figure, both methods can accomplish the task well, and the trajectory of move_base planning is better in some places. But it needs to be explained that move_base uses 360-dimensional laser scanning data, while the reinforcement learning model uses only 10-dimensional sparse laser scanning data. The result proves the effectiveness and superiority of the navigation method based on reinforcement learning.

In this article, a reinforcement learning method based on Soft Actor Critic was presented for mobile robot navigation in mapless environment. Continuous control of mobile robots was achieved by using 10-dimensional laser scanning data, target information, actions and rewards from the last time step as input. After a few hours of training, the method can achieve similar results to the traditional method. In addition, this continuous control method based on reinforcement learning can accomplish other more complex tasks. Of course, although it has achieved good results in the simulation environment, the application of virtual to real world still needs to be carried out in future work.
